lines: When trouble came in like a bad tide, you helped drag it back out.
You held the lane while we moved families toward the river.
The dock would have fallen if you had not reached it in time.
I saw you pull a villager clear before the next arrow landed.
You kept the raiders away from the boats.
The shield line held because you did not give ground.
We used the river as an escape route, and you kept that route open.
You warned us before the fighting reached the shore.
The village still has a boathouse because you stood in front of it.
You fought until the bells stopped and then helped count the missing.
I watched you carry the injured instead of chasing glory.
Your arrows gave us room to bar the doors.
The children reached shelter while you drew danger elsewhere.
You defended people who had little to offer you.
The dock bears the scars, but every boat is still ours.
You stayed when anyone could have run.
We had time to form a bucket line because you held the square.
You saw trouble on the far bank before the rest of us did.
The village owes you more than repairs and a warm meal.
I will remember who stood beside us when the water ran red.
